title: Quartermaster and Chemical Equipment Repairer (QM & Chem Equip Rep)
raw_text:
10-91J. MOS 91J--Quartermaster and Chemical Equipment Repairer (QM & Chem Equip
Rep), CMF 91
(Army Civilian Acquired Skills Program (ACASP) designated MOS) (Effective 202510)
    a. Major duties. The quartermaster and chemical equipment repairer supervises or performs
field level maintenance on chemical equipment, quartermaster machinery, forced air-heaters, and
special purpose equipment. Duties for MOS 91J at each skill level are:
         (1) MOSC 91J1O. Maintains and repairs electrical/fuel heater systems, liquid pumps and
pumping systems, tactical and lightweight reverse osmosis water purification systems,
decontamination systems, protective filter systems, smoke generator systems and laundry
systems. Maintain internal combustion engine ignition/fuel/cooling/electrical systems. Perform
battlefield damage assessment and repair (BDAR).
         (2) MOSC 91J2O. Performs duties in preceding skill level, supervises junior grade
Soldiers and provides technical guidance to the Soldiers in the accomplishment of their duties.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Quartermaster and
chemical equipment repairers must possess the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A physical profile of 222222.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Must possess finger dexterity in both hands.
         (5) Must not be allergic to petroleum related products.
         (6) Qualifying scores.
             (a) A minimum score of 87 MM or a combination of 82 MM and 85 GT.
            (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power
Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
         (5) Formal training by completion of MOS 91J course conducted under the auspices of the
USA Ordnance School is mandatory or meet civilian acquired skills criteria per paragraph
9-5(7)(b) of this pamphlet unless a waiver is approved by the Commandant, U.S. Army Ordnance
School.
         (6) ACASP qualification criteria. (Note: Refer to table 9-1 (MOS’ Approved for the Army
Civilian Acquired Skills Program (ACASP)).
    c. Additional skill identifiers. D6—Operational Data Analyst (personnel only) (Note: Refer to
table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all enlisted MOS)).
    d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following tables:
         (1) Table 10-91J-1. Physical requirements.
         (2) Table 10-91J-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (3) Table 10-91J-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
